evidence: only-tls-1-3-is-accepted @ manifests/nginx_frontend_domain.pp:92: the default $base_ssl_protocols_prefix is ['TLSv1.3'] and the fixture leaves additional_ssl_protocols at [] (line 311 concat, 313 join), so ssl_protocols is 'TLSv1.3'; the probe expects a TLS 1.3 handshake to complete ('New, TLSv1.3') and a TLS 1.2 one to be refused ('New, (NONE)'), which is what that list produces; the TLS 1.2 attempt is the in-check contrast that must fail

http-redirects-to-https @ manifests/nginx_frontend_domain.pp:453 (with 420): http_www.${domain} returns '301 https://www.${domain}$request_uri' and, with decorate_naked false (the fixture default), http_${domain} returns '301 https://${domain}$request_uri' (line 420); the probe expects 301 to https on the same name with path and query kept, for each of the two names, which matches $request_uri carrying both

only-tls-1-3-is-accepted @ manifests/nginx_frontend_domain.pp:695: ssl_protocols => $base_ssl_protocols sits on the main server https_www.${domain} (lines 684-712), which with decorate_naked false is the only 443 server (https_${domain} is ensure absent, lines 527-536), so a handshake to 127.0.0.1:443 with SNI www.p8test.example.com reaches that directive; the probe tests it

purpose covered: Purpose matches the header comments and code: a per-domain nginx TLS frontend (http naked/www servers redirecting to https, main https server for $domain and www.$domain proxying to the backend_${domain} upstream, with the domain cert and TLSv1.3-only). Tested on the applied node: both 301 redirects with path+query (lines 416-455), HTTPS on www and on the naked domain returning the backend's page through the upstream (409-412, 521-524, 564, 684-712), certificate verification against the bundle's issuer with a non-matching name (other.example.com) failing (the only 443 server would otherwise serve the page, so the empty result proves the name check), and TLS 1.3 accepted / 1.2 refused. Honestly uncovered: the RedHat key dir (272-283, lifted by rhel9) and non-default fixture variants. Ciphers, ecdh_curve and prefer_server_ciphers have no effect under TLSv1.3-only (header comment lines 87-91, 100, 113), so they are not observable. Notes: the variants row is not exhaustive (it does not name www_fix_redirect, enable_ssl false, domain_backend_pass_suffix/set_headers, proxy_locations_adhoc/others/ignore_headers, use_compact_log_format, server_https_www_create/redirect_http_www_to_https_www_create false, the Hash form of backend_hosts_and_ports and the fail() guards at 294-303); its stated reason (one fixture per set, all at defaults) applies to them equally. Outcome 1 also maps a-backend-answers, which is a setup step (a python backend on 127.0.0.1:8080) and probes no redirect; http-redirects-to-https alone covers it.
